G1199.def: a bond, anything by which one is bound, a cord, chain, fetters, etc.; and by meton. imprisonment, Lk. 8:29; Acts 16:26; 20:23; a string or ligament, as of the tongue, Mk. 7:35; met. an impediment, infirmity, Lk. 13:16

G1200.def: a keeper of a prison, jailer, Acts 16:23, 27, 36*

G1204.def: here; used also as a sort of imperative, come, Come here! Mt. 19:21; Mk. 10:21; used of time, ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, i.e. χρόνου, to the present time, Rom. 1:13

G1205.def: come, Mt. 4:19; 11:28; as a particle of exhortation, incitement, etc., and followed by an imperative, come now, etc., Mt. 21:38; 28:6

G1206.def: on the second day of a certain state or process, and used as an epithet of the subject or agent, Acts 28:13*

G1208.def: second, Mt. 22:26; τὸ δεύτερον, again, the second time, another time, Jude 5; so ἐκ δευτέρου, Mt. 26:42; and ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ, Acts 7:13

G1209.def: to take into one’s hands, etc., Lk. 2:28; 16:6, 7; to receive, Acts 22:5; 28:21; Phil. 4:18; to receive into and retain, contain, Acts 3:21; met. to receive by the hearing, learn, acquire a knowledge of, 2 Cor. 11:4; Jas. 1:21; to receive, admit, grant access to, receive kindly, welcome, Mt. 10:40, 41; 18:5; to receive in hospitality, entertain, Lk. 9:53; Heb. 11:31; to bear with, bear patiently, 2 Cor. 11:16; met. to receive, approve, assent to, Mt. 11:14; Lk. 8:13; Acts 8:14; 11:1; to admit, and by impl. to embrace, follow, 1 Cor. 2:14; 2 Cor. 8:17

G1210.def: to bind, tie, Mt. 13:30; 21:2; to bind, confine, Mt. 27:2; 14:3; to impede, hinder, 2 Tim. 2:9; to bind with infirmity, Lk. 13:16; to bind by a legal or moral tie, as marriage, Rom. 7:2; 1 Cor. 7:27, 39; by impl. to impel, compel, Acts 20:22; in NT to pronounce or declare to be binding or obligatory, or, to declare to be prohibited and unlawful, Mt. 16:19; 18:18

G1211.def: a particle that adds an intensity of expression to a term or clause. Its simplest and most ordinary uses are when it gives impressiveness to an affirmation, indeed, really, doubtless, Mt. 13:23; or earnestness to a call, injunction, or entreaty, Lk. 2:15; Acts 13:2; 15:36; 1 Cor. 16:20*

G1212.def: pr. clearly visible; plain, manifest, evident, Mt. 26:73; 1 Cor. 15:27; Gal. 3:11*

G1213.def: to render manifest or evident; to make known, to tell, relate, declare, 1 Cor. 1:11; Col. 1:8; to show, point out, bring to light, 1 Cor. 3:13; to indicate, signify, Heb. 9:8; 12:27; 1 Pet. 1:11

G1214.def: Demas, pr. name, Col. 4:14; 2 Tim. 4:10; Phlm. 24*

G1215.def: to address a public assembly, to deliver a public oration, Acts 12:21*

G1216.def: Demetrius, pr. name (1) The Ephesian silversmith, Acts 19:24, 38 (2) A certain Christian, 3 Jn. 12*

G1217.def: pr. one who labors for the public, or, exercises some public calling; an architect, especially, the Divine Architect of the universe, Heb. 11:10

G1219.def: public, belonging to the public, Acts 5:18; δημοσίᾳ, publicly, Acts 16:37; 18:28; 20:20*

G1220.def: Latin denarius, a Roman silver coin; the name originally meant ten asses, Mt. 18:28; Mk. 6:37; Rev. 6:6

G1222.def: now in some way, surely, Heb. 2:16*

G1223.def: (1) gen., through, used of place or medium, Mt. 7:13; Lk. 6:1; 2 Cor. 11:33; through, of time, during, in the course of, Heb. 2:15; Acts 5:19; through, of immediate agency, causation, instrumentality, by means of, by, Jn. 1:3; Acts 3:18; of means or manner, through, by, with, Lk. 8:4; 2 Cor. 5:7; 8:8; of state or condition, in a state of, Rom. 4:11; (2) acc., used of causation which is not direct and immediate in the production of a result, on account of, because of, for the sake of, with a view to, Mk. 2:27; Jn. 1:31; rarely, through, while subject to a state of untoward circumstances, Gal. 4:13

G1224.def: to pass through or over, Lk. 16:26; Acts 16:9; Heb. 11:29*

G1225.def: to throw or convey through or over; to thrust through; to defame, inform against, Lk. 16:1*

G1226.def: to assert strongly, insist, 1 Tim. 1:7; Tit. 3:8*

G1227.def: to look through; to view steadily, Mk. 8:25; to see clearly or steadily, Mt. 7:5; Lk. 6:42*

G1228.def: slanderer, 1 Tim. 3:11; 2 Tim. 3:3; Tit. 2:3; a treacherous informer, traitor, Jn. 6:70; ὁ διάβολος, the devil

G1229.def: to publish abroad, Lk. 9:60; Rom. 9:17; to certify to the public, Acts 21:26*

G1230.def: pass., to continue through; to intervene, elapse of time, Mk. 16:1; Acts 25:13; 27:9*

G1233.def: pr. an act of distinguishing or discernment; a determination; examination judicially, hearing, trial, Acts 25:21*

G1235.def: to remain awake; to wake thoroughly, Lk. 9:32*

G1236.def: to conduct or carry through or over; to pass or spend time, live, 1 Tim. 2:2; Tit. 3:3*

G1237.def: to receive by transmission; to receive in return, Acts 7:45*

G1241.def: to gird firmly round, Jn. 13:4, 5; mid. to gird round one’s self, Jn. 21:7*

G1242.def: a testamentary disposition, will; a covenant, Heb. 9:16, 17; Gal. 3:15; in NT, a covenant of God with men, Gal. 3:17; 4:24; Heb. 9:4; Mt. 26:28; the writings of the old covenant, 2 Cor. 3:14

G1243.def: a division; a distinction, difference, diversity, 1 Cor. 12:4, 5, 6*

G1244.def: to divide, to divide out, distribute, Lk. 15:12; 1 Cor. 12:11*

G1246.def: to maintain discussion strenuously and thoroughly, to totally refute, Acts 18:28*

G1248.def: serving, service, waiting, attendance, the act of rendering friendly offices, Lk. 10:40; 2 Tim. 4:11; Heb. 1:14; relief, aid, Acts 6:1; 11:29; 2 Cor. 8:4; 9:1, 12, 13; a commission, Acts 12:25; Rom. 15:31; a commission or ministry in the service of the Gospel, Acts 1:17, 25; 20:24; Rom. 11:13; 2 Cor. 4:1; 5:18; 1 Tim. 1:12; service in the Gospel, Acts 6:4; 21:19; 1 Cor. 16:15; 2 Cor. 6:3; 11:8; Eph. 4:12; Rev. 2:19; a function, ministry, or office in the Church, Rom. 12:7; 1 Cor. 12:5; Col. 4:17; 2 Tim. 4:5; a ministering in the conveyance of a revelation from God, 2 Cor. 3:7, 8, 9

G1257.def: to leave an interval; to intermit, cease, Lk. 7:45*

G1258.def: speech; manner of speaking; peculiar language of a nation, dialect, vernacular idiom, Acts 1:19; 2:6, 8; 21:40; 22:2; 26:14

G1259.def: to be reconciled to another, Mt. 5:24*

G1260.def: pr. to make a settlement of accounts; to reason, deliberate, ponder, consider, Mt. 16:7, 8; Mk. 2:6, 8; Jn. 11:50; to dispute, contend, Mk. 9:33

G1261.def: reasoning, thought, cogitation, purpose, Mt. 15:19; Mk. 7:21; discourse, dispute, disputation, contention, Lk. 9:46; doubt, hesitation, scruple, Lk. 24:38

G1263.def: to make solemn affirmation, protest; to make a solemn and earnest charge, Lk. 16:28; Acts 2:40; to declare solemnly and earnestly, Acts 8:25; 18:5

G1264.def: to fight out, to fight resolutely; met. to contend vehemently, insist, Acts 23:9*

G1265.def: to continue throughout; to continue, be permanent or unchanged, Lk. 1:22; Gal. 2:5; Heb. 1:11; 2 Pet. 3:4; to continue, remain constant, Lk. 22:28

G1267.def: division; met. in NT disunion, dissension, Lk. 12:51*

G1268.def: to distribute; to divulge, spread abroad, Acts 4:17*

G1269.def: to signify by a nod, beckon, make signs, Lk. 1:22*

G1276.def: to pass through or over, Mt. 9:1; 14:34; Mk. 5:21; 6:53; Lk. 16:26; Acts 21:2*

G1277.def: to sail through or over, Acts 27:5*

G1278.def: pr. to be thoroughly exercised with labor; to be wearied; to be vexed, Acts 4:2; 16:18*

G1296.def: an injunction, institute, ordinance, Rom. 13:2; Acts 7:53*

G1298.def: to throw into a state of perturbation, to move or trouble greatly, Lk. 1:29*

G1309.def: to flee through, escape by flight, Acts 27:42*

G1313.def: different, diverse, of different kinds, Rom. 12:6; Heb. 9:10; excellent, superior, Heb. 1:4; 8:6*

G1317.def: apt or qualified to teach, 1 Tim. 3:2; 2 Tim. 2:24*

G1322.def: instruction, the giving of instruction, teaching, Mk. 4:2; 12:38; instruction, what is taught, doctrine, Mt. 16:12; Jn. 7:16, 17; meton. mode of teaching and kind of doctrine taught, Mt. 7:28; Mk. 1:27

G1324.def: a twin; Didymus, the Greek equivalent to the name Thomas, Jn. 11:16; 20:24; 21:2*

G1327.def: a passage throughout; a line of road, a thoroughfare, Mt. 22:9*

G1329.def: to explain, interpret, translate, Lk. 24:27; Acts 9:36; 1 Cor. 14:5, 13, 27; to be able to interpret, 1 Cor. 12:30*

G1330.def: to pass through, Mk. 10:25; Lk. 4:30; to pass over, cross, Mk. 4:35; Lk. 8:22; to pass along, Lk. 19:4; to proceed, Lk. 2:15; Acts 9:38; to travel through or over a country, wander about, Mt. 12:43; Lk. 9:6; to transfix, pierce, Lk. 2:35; to spread abroad, be prevalent, as a rumor, Lk. 5:15; met. to extend to, Rom. 5:12

G1333.def: the space of two years, Acts 24:27; 28:30*

G3782.def: a debt, Mt. 18:32; met. a duty, due, Rom. 13:7; 1 Cor. 7:3*

G3783.def: a debt; a due, Rom. 4:4, in NT a delinquency, offence, fault, sin, Mt. 6:12, cf. v. 14*

G3784.def: to owe, be indebted, Mt. 18:28, 30, 34; to incur a bond, to be bound to make discharge, Mt. 23:16, 18; to be bound or obliged by what is due or fitting or consequently necessary, Lk. 17:10; Jn. 13:14; to incur desert, to deserve, Jn. 19:7; to be due or fitting, 1 Cor. 7:3, 36; from the Aramaic, to be delinquent, Lk. 11:4

G3785.def: originally a ptcp (aor act ptcp nom sg neut) from ὀφείλω, used in NT as an interj. to introduce a wish that cannot be attained, O that! Would that! 1 Cor. 4:8; 2 Cor. 11:1; Gal. 5:12; Rev. 3:15*

G3787.def: also written ὀφθαλμοδουλεία, eye-service, service rendered only while under inspection, Eph. 6:6; Col. 3:22*

G3788.def: an eye, Mt. 5:29, 38; 6:23; 7:3, 4, 5; ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός, an evil eye, an envious eye, envy, Mt. 20:15; Mk. 7:22; met. the intellectual eye, Mt. 13:15; Mk. 8:18; Jn. 12:40; Acts 26:18

G3789.def: a serpent, Mt. 7:10; 10:16; an artificial serpent, Jn. 3:14; used of the devil or Satan, Rev. 12:9, 14, 15; 20:2; met. a man of serpentine character, Mt. 23:33

G3790.def: a brow, eye-brow; the brow of a mountain, edge of a precipice, Lk. 4:29*

G3791.def: pr. to mob; to disturb, trouble, Acts 5:16*

G3792.def: to collect a mob, create a tumult, Acts 17:5*

G3793.def: a crowd, a confused multitude of people, Mt. 4:25; 5:1; 7:28; spc. the common people, Jn. 7:49; a multitude, great number, Lk. 5:29; 6:17; Acts 1:15; by impl. tumult, uproar, Lk. 22:6; Acts 24:18

G3794.def: a stronghold; met. an opposing bulwark of error or vice, 2 Cor. 10:4*

G3796.def: can function as an improper prep., late; put for the first watch, at evening, Mk. 11:19; 13:35; ὀψὲ σαββάτων, after the close of the Sabbath, Mt. 28:1

G3798.def: evening, either before or after sundown

G3797.def: late; latter, Jas. 5:7; poetic and later prose for ὄψιος*

G3799.def: a sight; the face, countenance, Jn. 11:44; Rev. 1:16; external appearance, Jn. 7:24*

G3800.def: provisions; a stipend or pay of soldiers, Lk. 3:14; 1 Cor. 9:7; wages of any kind, 2 Cor. 11:8; due wages, a stated recompense, Rom. 6:23*

G3803.def: a snare, trap, Lk. 21:35; met. device, wile, 1 Tim. 3:7; 6:9; 2 Tim. 2:26; met. a trap of ruin, Rom. 11:9*

G0697.def: a hill, Ἄρειος πάγος, Areopagus, the hill of Mars, at Athens, Acts 17:19, 22. See PhotoGuide.

G3804.def: what is suffered; suffering, affliction, Rom. 8:18; 2 Cor. 1:5, 6, 7; Phil. 3:10; emotion, passion, Rom. 7:5; Gal. 5:24

G3805.def: passible, capable of suffering, liable to suffer; in NT destined to suffer, Acts 26:23*

G3806.def: suffering; an affection, passion, especially sexual, Rom. 1:26

G3807.def: a pedagogue, childtender, a person, usually a slave or freedman, to whom the care of the boys of a family was committed, whose duty it was to attend them at their play, lead them to and from the public school, and exercise a constant superintendence over their conduct and safety; in NT an ordinary director or minister contrasted with an Apostle, as a pedagogue occupies an inferior position to a parent, 1 Cor. 4:15; a term applied to the Mosaic law, as dealing with men as in a state of mere childhood and tutelage, Gal. 3:24, 25*

G3808.def: a little boy, child; a boy, lad, Jn. 6:9*

G3809.def: education, training up, nurture of children, Eph. 6:4; instruction, discipline, 2 Tim. 3:16; in NT correction, chastisement, Heb. 12:5, 7, 8, 11*

G3810.def: a preceptor, instructor, teacher, pr. of boys; genr. Rom. 2:20; in NT a chastiser, Heb. 12:9*

G3811.def: to educate, instruct children, Acts 7:22; 22:3; genr. παιδεύομαι, to be taught, learn, 1 Tim. 1:20; to admonish, instruct by admonition, 2 Tim. 2:25; Tit. 2:12; in NT to chastise, chasten, 1 Cor. 11:32; 2 Cor. 6:9; Heb. 12:6, 7, 10; Rev. 3:19; of criminals, to scourge, Lk. 23:16, 22*

G3812.def: from childhood, from a child, Mk. 9:21*

G3813.def: an infant, babe, Mt. 2:8; but usually in NT as equiv. to παῖς, Mt. 14:21; Mk. 7:28, et al. freq.; pl. voc. used by way of endearment, my dear children, 1 Jn. 2:18; also as a term of familiar address, children, my lads, Jn. 21:5

G3814.def: a girl, damsel, maiden; a female slave or servant, Mt. 26:69; Mk. 14:66, 69

G3815.def: to play in the manner of children; to sport, to practise the festive gestures of idolatrous worship, 1 Cor. 10:7*

G3816.def: a child in relation to parents, of either sex, Jn. 4:51; a child in respect of age, either male or female, and of all ages from infancy up to manhood, a boy, youth, girl, maiden, Mt. 2:16; 17:18; Lk. 2:43; 8:54; a servant, slave, Mt. 8:6, 8, 13, cf. v. 9; Lk. 7:7, cf. v. 3, 10; an attendant, minister, Mt. 14:2; Lk. 1:69; Acts 4:25; also, Lk. 1:54; or, perhaps, a child in respect of fatherly regard

G3817.def: to strike, smite, with the fist, Mt. 26:68; Lk. 22:64; with a sword, Mk. 14:47; Jn. 18:10; to strike as a scorpion, to sting, Rev. 9:5*

G3819.def: of old, long ago, Mt. 11:21; Lk. 10:13; Heb. 1:1; Jude 4; οἱ πάλαι, old, former, 2 Pet. 1:9; some time since, already, Mk. 15:44

G3820.def: old, not new or recent, Mt. 9:16, 17; 13:52; Lk. 5:36

G3822.def: to make old; pass. to grow old, to become worn, Lk. 12:33; Heb. 1:11; met. to treat as antiquated, to abrogate, supersede, Heb. 8:13*

G3824.def: a new birth; regeneration, renovation, Mt. 19:28; Tit. 3:5. See unpublished Ph.D. dissertation, William D. Mounce, The Origin of the New Testament Metaphor of Rebirth, University of Aberdeen, Scotland*

G3825.def: pr. back; again, back again, Jn. 10:17; Acts 10:16; 11:10; again by repetition, Mt. 26:43; again in continuation, further, Mt. 5:33; 13:44, 45, 47, 18:19; again, on the other hand, 1 Jn. 2:8

G3826.def: the whole multitude together, all at once, Lk. 23:18*

G3828.def: Pamphylia, a country of Asia Minor, Acts 2:10; 13:13; 14:24; 15:38; 27:5*

G3829.def: a public inn, place where travelers may lodge, called in the East by the name of menzil, khan, caravanserai, Lk. 10:34*

G3830.def: the keeper of a public inn or caravanserai, a host, Lk. 10:35*

G3831.def: pr. an assembly of an entire people; a solemn gathering at a festival; a festive convocation, Heb. 12:22*

G3832.def: also spelled πανοικί, with one’s whole household or family, Acts 16:34*

G3833.def: panoply, complete armor, a complete suit of armor, both offensive and defensive, as the shield, sword, spear, helmet, breastplate, etc., Lk. 11:22; Eph. 6:11, 13*

G3835.def: pr. ready to do anything; hence, crafty, cunning, artful, wily, 2 Cor. 12:16*

G3837.def: in all places, everywhere, Mk. 16:20; Lk. 9:6

G3838.def: perfect, complete; εἰς τὸ παντελές, adverbially, throughout, through all time, ever, Heb. 7:25; with a negative, at all, Lk. 13:11*

G3839.def: everywhere; in every way, in every instance, Acts 24:3*

G3840.def: from every place, from all parts, on all sides, on every side, round about, Mk. 1:45; Lk. 19:43; Heb. 9:4*

G3842.def: always, at all times, ever, Mt. 26:11; Mk. 14:7; Lk. 15:31; 18:1

G3843.def: wholly, altogether; at any rate, by all means, 1 Cor. 9:22; by impl. surely, assuredly, certainly, Lk. 4:23; Acts 21:22; 28:4; 1 Cor. 9:10; οὐ πάντως, in nowise, not in the least, Rom. 3:9; 1 Cor. 5:10; 16:12*

G3844.def: (1) gen., from, indicating source or origin, Mt. 2:4, 7; Mk. 8:11; Lk. 2:1; οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῦ, his relatives or kinsmen, Mk. 3:21; τὰ παρ’ αὐτῆς πάντα, all her substance, property, etc., Mk. 5:26. (2) dat., with, in, among, etc., Mt. 6:1; 19:26; 21:25; 22:25; παρ’ ἑαυτῷ, at home, 1 Cor. 16:2; in the sight of, in the judgment or estimation of, 1 Cor. 3:19; 2 Pet. 2:11; 3:8. (3) acc., motion, by, near to, along, Mt. 4:18; motion, towards, to, at, Mt. 15:30; Mk. 2:13; motion terminating in rest, at, by, near, by the side of, Mk. 4:1, 4; Lk. 5:1; 8:5; in deviation from, in violation of, inconsistently with, Acts 18:13; Rom. 1:26; 11:24; above, more than, Lk. 13:2, 4; Rom. 1:25. (4) Misc., after comparatives, Lk. 3:13; 1 Cor. 3:11; except, save, 2 Cor. 11:24; beyond, past, Heb. 11:11; in respect of, on the score of, 1 Cor. 12:15, 16

G3845.def: pr. to step by the side of; to deviate; met. to transgress, violate, Mt. 15:2, 3; to incur forfeiture, Acts 1:25*

G3846.def: to cast or throw by the side of; absol., a nautical term, to bring to, land, Acts 20:15*

G3847.def: a stepping by the side, deviation; a transgression, violation of law, Rom. 2:23; 4:15

G3848.def: transgressor, violator of law, Rom. 2:25, 27; Gal. 2:18; Jas. 2:9, 11*

G3849.def: to force; to constrain press with urgent entreaties, Lk. 24:29; Acts 16:15*

G3850.def: a placing one thing by the side of another; a comparing; a parallel case cited in illustration; a comparison, simile, similitude, Mk. 4:30; Heb. 11:19; a parable, a short relation under which something else is figured, or in which that which is fictitious is employed to represent that which is real, Mt. 13:3, 10, 13, 18, 24, 31, 33, 34, 36, 53; 21:33, 45; 22:1; 24:32; in NT a type, pattern, emblem, Heb. 9:9; a sentiment, grave and significant precept, maxim, Lk. 14:7; an obscure and enigmatical saying, anything expressed in remote and ambiguous terms, Mt. 13:35; Mk. 7:17; a proverb, adage, Lk. 4:23

G3852.def: a command, order, charge, Acts 5:28; 16:24; direction, precept, 1 Thess. 4:2; 1 Tim. 1:5, 18*

G3853.def: to announce, notify; to command, direct, charge, Mt. 10:5; Mk. 6:8, 8:6; Lk. 9:21; to charge, entreat solemnly, 1 Tim. 6:13

G3854.def: pluperfect, παραγεγόνει (3 sg), to be by the side of; to come, approach, arrive, Mt. 2:1; 3:13; Mk. 14:43; Lk. 7:4; seq. ἐπί, to come upon in order to seize, Lk. 22:52; to come forth in public, make appearance, Mt. 3:1; Heb. 9:11

G3855.def: to lead beside; intrans. to pass along or by, Mt. 20:30; Jn. 9:1; to pass on, Mt. 9:9, 27; intrans. and mid. to pass away, be in a state of transition, 1 Cor. 7:31; 1 Jn. 2:8, 17

G3856.def: to make an example of; to expose to ignominy and shame, Heb. 6:6*

G3857.def: a park, a forest where wild beasts were kept for hunting; a pleasure-park, a garden of trees of various kinds; used in the LXX for the Garden of Eden; in NT the celestial paradise, Lk. 23:43; 2 Cor. 12:4; Rev. 2:7*

G3858.def: to accept, receive, met. to receive, admit, yield assent to, Mk. 4:20; Acts 15:4; 16:21; 22:18; 1 Tim. 5:19; in NT to receive or embrace with favor, approve, love, Heb. 12:6*

G3860.def: pluperfect, παραδεδώκεισαν (3 pl), to give over, hand over, deliver up, Mt. 4:12; 5:25; 10:4, 17; to commit, intrust, Mt. 11:27; 25:14; to commit, commend, Acts 14:26; 15:40; to yield up, Jn. 19:30; 1 Cor. 15:24; to abandon, Acts 7:42; Eph. 4:19; to stake, hazard, Acts 15:26; to deliver as a matter of injunction, instruction, etc., Mk. 7:13; Lk. 1:2; Acts 6:14; absol. to render a yield, to be matured, Mk. 4:29

G3862.def: delivery, handing over, transmission; in NT what is transmitted in the way of teaching, precept, doctrine, 1 Cor. 11:2; 2 Thess. 2:15; 3:6; tradition, traditionary law, handed down from age to age, Mt. 15:2, 3, 6

G3863.def: to provoke to jealousy, Rom. 10:19; to excite to emulation, Rom. 11:11, 14; to provoke to indignation, 1 Cor. 10:22*

G3864.def: by the sea-side, situated on the sea-coast, maritime, Mt. 4:13*

G3865.def: to look at things placed side by side, as in comparison, to compare in thus looking, to regard less in comparison, overlook, neglect, Acts 6:1*

G3866.def: a deposit, a thing committed to one’s charge, a trust, 1 Tim. 6:20; 2 Tim. 1:12; 2 Tim. 1:14*

G3868.def: to entreat; to beg off, excuse one’s self, Lk. 14:18, 19; to deprecate, entreat against, Acts 25:11; Heb. 12:19; to decline receiving, refuse, reject, 1 Tim. 4:7; 5:11; Tit. 3:10; Heb. 12:25; to decline, avoid, shun, 2 Tim. 2:23

G3870.def: to call for, invite to come, send for, Acts 28:20; to call upon, exhort, admonish, persuade, Lk. 3:18; Acts 2:40; 11:23; to beg, beseech, entreat, implore, Mt. 8:5, 31; 18:29; Mk. 1:40; to animate, encourage, comfort, console, Mt. 2:18; 5:4; 2 Cor. 1:4, 6; pass. to be cheered, comforted, Lk. 16:25; Acts 20:12; 2 Cor. 7:13

G3871.def: to cover over, veil; met. pass. to be veiled from comprehension, Lk. 9:45*

G3873.def: to lie near, be adjacent; met. to be at hand, be present, Rom. 7:18, 21*

G3874.def: a calling upon, exhortation, incitement, persuasion, Rom. 12:8; 1 Cor. 14:3; hortatory instruction, Acts 13:15; 15:31; entreaty, importunity, earnest supplication, 2 Cor. 8:4; solace, consolation, Lk. 2:25; Rom. 15:4, 5; 2 Cor. 1:3, 4, 5, 6, 7; cheering and supporting influence, Acts 9:31; joy, gladness, rejoicing, 2 Cor. 7:13; cheer, joy, enjoyment, Lk. 6:24

G3875.def: one called or sent for to assist another; an advocate, one who pleads the cause of another, 1 Jn. 2:1; genr. one present to render various beneficial service, and thus the Paraclete, whose influence and operation were to compensate for the departure of Christ himself, Jn. 14:16, 26; 15:26; 16:7*

G3876.def: an erroneous or imperfect hearing; disobedience, Rom. 5:19; a deviation from obedience, 2 Cor. 10:6; Heb. 2:2*

G3877.def: to follow or accompany closely; to accompany, attend, characterize, Mk. 16:17; to follow with the thoughts, trace, Lk. 1:3; to conform to, 1 Tim. 4:6; 2 Tim. 3:10*

G3878.def: to overhear, Mk. 5:36; to hear amiss, to fail to listen, neglect to obey, disregard, Mt. 18:17 (2x)*

G3879.def: to stoop beside; to stoop down in order to take a view, Lk. 24:12; Jn. 20:5, 11; to bestow a close and attentive look, to look intently, to penetrate, Jas. 1:25; 1 Pet. 1:12*

G3880.def: pr. to take to one’s side; to take, receive to one’s self, Mt. 1:20; Jn. 14:3; to take with one’s self, Mt. 2:13, 14, 20, 21; 4:5, 8; to receive in charge or possession, Col. 4:17; Heb. 12:28; to receive as a matter of instruction, Mk. 7:4; 1 Cor. 11:23; 15:3; to receive, admit, acknowledge, Jn. 1:11; 1 Cor. 15:1; Col. 2:6; pass. to be carried off, Mt. 24:40, 41; Lk. 17:34, 35, 36

G3881.def: to gather a course along; to sail by, coast along, Acts 27:8, 13*

G3882.def: adjacent to the sea, maritime; ἡ παράλιος, i.e. χώρα, the sea coast, Lk. 6:17*

G3884.def: to misreckon, make a false reckoning; to impose upon, deceive, delude, circumvent, Col. 2:4; Jas. 1:22*

G3885.def: lame, palsied, used only as a noun in NT, paralytic, Mt. 4:24; 8:6; 9:2, 6

G3886.def: to unloose from proper fixity or consistency of substance; to enervate or paralyze the body or limbs; pass. to be enervated or enfeebled, Heb. 12:12; pass. perf. part. παραλελυμένος, paralytic, Lk. 5:18, 24

G3887.def: to stay beside; to continue, stay, abide, 1 Cor. 16:6; Heb. 7:23; met. to remain constant in, persevere in, Phil. 1:25; Jas. 1:25*

G3888.def: to exercise a gentle influence by words; to soothe, comfort, console, Jn. 11:19, 31; 1 Thess. 5:14; to cheer, exhort, 1 Thess. 2:12*

G3891.def: to violate or transgress the law, Acts 23:3*

G3892.def: violation of the law, transgression, 2 Pet. 2:16*

G3893.def: pr. to incite to bitter feelings; to provoke; absol. to act provokingly, be rebellious, Heb. 3:16*

G3895.def: pr. to fall by the side of; met. to fall off or away from, make defection from, Heb. 6:6*

G3896.def: to sail by or past a place, Acts 20:16*

G3897.def: pr. near alongside; met. like, similar; neut. παραπλήσιον, adverbially, near to, nearly, with a near approach to, Phil. 2:27*

G3898.def: like, in the same or like manner, Heb. 2:14*

G3899.def: to pass by the side of; to pass along, Mt. 27:39; Mk. 2:23; 9:30; 11:20; 15:29*

G3900.def: pr. a stumbling aside, a false step; in NT a trespass, fault, offence, transgression, Mt. 6:14, 15; Mk. 11:25, 26; Rom. 4:25; a fall in faith, Rom. 11:11, 12

G3901.def: to flow beside; to glide aside from; to fall off from profession, decline from steadfastness, make forfeit of faith, Heb. 2:1*

G3902.def: a distinguishing mark; an ensign of a ship, Acts 28:11*

G3903.def: to prepare, make ready, 2 Cor. 9:2, 3; mid. to prepare one’s self, put one’s self in readiness, Acts 10:10; 1 Cor. 14:8*

G3904.def: a getting ready, preparation, in NT preparation for a feast, day of preparation, Mt. 27:62; Mk. 15:42

G3905.def: to extend, stretch out; to prolong, continue, Acts 20:7*

G3906.def: to watch narrowly, Acts 9:24; to observe or watch insidiously, Mk. 3:2; Lk. 6:7; 14:1; 20:20; to observe scrupulously, Gal. 4:10*

G3908.def: to place by the side of, or near; to set before, Mk. 6:41; 8:6, 7; Lk. 9:16; met. to set or lay before, propound, Mt. 13:24, 31; to inculcate, Acts 17:3; to deposit, commit to the charge of, entrust, Lk. 12:48; 23:46; to commend, Acts 14:23

G3909.def: to happen, to chance upon, chance to meet, Acts 17:17*

G3910.def: instantly, immediately; ὁ, ἡ, τό, παραυτίκα, momentary, transient, 2 Cor. 4:17*

G3911.def: to carry past; to cause to pass away, Mk. 14:36; Lk. 22:42; pass. to be swept along, Jude 12; to be led away, misled, seduced, Heb. 13:9*

G3912.def: to be beside one’s wits; παραφρονῶν, in foolish style, 2 Cor. 11:23*

G3914.def: to winter, spend the winter, Acts 27:12; 28:11; 1 Cor. 16:6; Tit. 3:12*

G3915.def: a wintering in a place, Acts 27:12*

G4332.def: to sit near; to attend, serve, 1 Cor. 9:13*

G3918.def: to be beside; to be present, Lk. 13:1; to have come, Mt. 26:50; Jn. 7:6; 11:28; Col. 1:6; to be in possession, Heb. 13:5; 2 Pet. 1:9, 12; part. παρών, οῦσα, όν, present, 1 Cor. 5:3; τὸ παρόν, the present time, the present, Heb. 12:11

G3920.def: secretly introduced, brought in stealthily, Gal. 2:4*

G3922.def: to supervene, Rom. 5:20; to steal in, Gal. 2:4*

G3923.def: to bring in beside; to bring into play, exhibit in addition, 2 Pet. 1:5*

G3924.def: can function as an improper prep., without, on the outside; except, Mt. 5:32; Acts 26:29; τὰ παρεκτός, other matters, 2 Cor. 11:28

G3925.def: an insertion besides; later, a marshalling of an army; an array of battle, army, Heb. 11:34; a camp, Heb. 13:11, 13; Rev. 20:9; a standing camp, fortress, citadel, castle, Acts 21:34, 37; 22:24; 23:10, 16, 32*

G3927.def: residing in a country not one’s own, a sojourner, stranger, Heb. 11:13; 1 Pet. 1:1; 2:11*

G3928.def: to pass beside, pass along, pass by, Mt. 8:28; Mk. 6:48; to pass, elapse, as time, Mt. 14:15; Acts 27:19; to pass away, be removed, Mt. 26:39, 42; Mk. 14:35; met. to pass away, disappear, vanish, perish, Mt. 5:18; 24:34, 35; to become vain, be rendered void, Mt. 5:18; Mk. 13:31; trans. to pass by, disregard, neglect, Lk. 11:42; 15:29; to come to the side of, come to, Lk. 12:37; 17:7

G3929.def: a letting pass; a passing over, Rom. 3:25*

G3930.def: to hold beside; to hold out to, offer, present, Lk. 6:29; to confer, render, Lk. 7:4; Acts 22:2; 28:2; Col. 4:1; to afford, furnish, Acts 16:16; 17:31; 19:24; 1 Tim. 6:17; to exhibit, Tit. 2:7; to be the cause of, occasion, Mt. 26:10; Mk. 14:6; Lk. 11:7

G3933.def: a virgin, maid, Mt. 1:23; 25:1, 7, 11; Acts 21:9; in NT also masc., chaste, Rev. 14:4

G3934.def: a Parthian, a native of Parthia, in central Asia, Acts 2:9

G3935.def: to let pass beside, let fall beside; to relax, Lk. 11:42; perf. pass. part. παρειμένος, hanging down helplessly, unstrung, feeble, Heb. 12:12*

G3936.def: pluperfect, παρειστήκειν, also formed as παριστάνω, trans. to place beside; to have in readiness, provide, Acts 23:24; to range beside, to place at the disposal of, Mt. 26:53; Acts 9:41; to present to God, dedicate, consecrate, devote, Lk. 2:22; Rom. 6:13, 19; to prove, demonstrate, show, Acts 1:3; 24:13; to commend, recommend, 1 Cor. 8:8; intrans. perf. παρέστηκα, part. παρεστώς, pluperf. παρειστήκειν, 2 aor. παρέστην, and mid., to stand by or before, Acts 27:24; Rom. 14:10; to stand by, to be present, Mk. 14:47, 69, 70; to stand in attendance, attend, Lk. 1:19; 1:24; of time, to be present, have come, Mk. 4:29; to stand by in aid, assist, support, Rom. 16:2

G3938.def: a way by; a passing by; ἐν παρόδῳ, in passing, by the way, 1 Cor. 16:7*

G3939.def: to dwell beside; later, to reside in a place as a stranger, sojourn, be a stranger or sojourner, Lk. 24:18; Heb. 11:9*

G3940.def: a sojourning, temporary residence in a foreign land, Acts 13:17; 1 Pet. 1:17*

G3941.def: a neighbor; later, a sojourner, temporary resident, stranger, Acts 7:6, 29; Eph. 2:19; 1 Pet. 2:11*

G3942.def: a by-word, proverb, adage, 2 Pet. 2:22; in NT an obscure saying, enigma, Jn. 16:25, 29; a parable, similitude, figurative discourse, Jn. 10:6*

G3943.def: pr. pertaining to wine, drunken; hence, quarrelsome, insolent, overbearing, 1 Tim. 3:3; Tit. 1:7*

G3944.def: to have gone by; perf. part. παρῳχημένος, by-gone, Acts 14:16*

to institute the celebration of a festival, Heb. 11:28; ποιεῖν τινα ἔχω, to cause to leave a place, i.q. ἔχω ἄγειν, to lead or conduct out, Acts 5:34; to pass, spend time, continue for a time, Mt. 20:12;
